office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, labor law and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: A 2024 rematch: Republican Rep. Gloria Mendoza, a former Grandview mayor, faces Democrat Chelsea Dimas of Sunnyside. They split on taxes, the Climate Commitment Act, school funding, data centers and state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

candidates.summary: One-term State Representative, former Grandview mayor and founder of a vocational-training business, running on lower taxes, budget restraint and repeal of the Climate Commitment Act.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O, services and transportation revenue bills [S4][S5][S6][S7]
Would "get rid of the Climate Commitment Act"; voted against the 2025 clean fuels bill [S16][S9]
Voted against the 2025 amendments to the parental-rights law and wrote in support of parents' record-access and notification rights [S8][S18]
Says she is "in the middle" on data centers and wants more study [S15]

taxes.basis: No votes on ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081, ESSB 5814 and ESSB 5801; statements opposing new taxes and calling for eliminating taxes on food and diapers.

spending.basis: Says the state should keep what it has without increasing the budget, voted no on the 2025 operating budget, and pledges to stop runaway government spending.

climate.basis: Calls for repealing the Climate Commitment Act over fuel costs; voted against the 2025 clean fuels program bill.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases; blames energy policies imposed on developers for home prices.

safety.basis: Called to 'finally fund the police' and for tougher theft and fentanyl penalties; campaigns on safer streets. She voted against the 2025 public safety funding bill, which carried a local option tax (S13).

immigration.basis: Voted twice against the 2026 immigrant worker protections bill; no statement on immigration found.

tech.basis: Undecided on data centers and open to their local benefits; voted against the 2026 bill addressing large energy use facilities.

social.basis: Voted against the 2026 bill improving access to abortion medications; statement says she defends family values.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 twice and wrote that she fought for parents' access to records, review of materials and notifications.

experience.basis: Incumbent legislator and Assistant Minority Whip with eight prior years as a Grandview council member and mayor.

candidates.summary: Sunnyside nonprofit worker and former state commissioner on human rights and Hispanic affairs, running a second time on affordability, school funding, workers' rights and protection of immigrant families.
highlights: Calls the millionaire's tax "a great path forward" [S5]
"Completely against data centers" until regulations are in place [S4]
Would keep state and local resources out of federal immigration enforcement [S2]
Supports more school funding, universal childcare and collective bargaining for farmworkers [S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Calls the millionaire's tax a great path forward while wanting tax relief for working people.

spending.basis: Fully supports $2 billion more for schools, more mental-health and support staff, and universal childcare.

housing.basis: Would build affordable housing, strengthen renter protections and expand down-payment assistance, while also citing more supply.

safety.basis: Pairs officer recruitment with behavioral-health and crisis response and prevention of violence and addiction.

climate.basis: Supports clean-energy investment and climate preparedness; withdrew support for the 2025 gas tax over costs to working people.

immigration.basis: Would bar state and local resources from federal immigration enforcement and supports labor rights regardless of immigration status.

tech.basis: Completely against data centers; wants a ban until regulations protect water and utility ratepayers.

social.basis: Would protect access to reproductive health care and care regardless of gender identity; no further positions found.

experience.basis: No prior public office beyond precinct committee officer; criticizes 30 years of 'recycled leadership' in the district.
